hook.line: Sunday night, three hundred tintos later, Hernando's friends are heading home. A plain *gracias* is fine, but you want to say what you're thankful for, and that takes one small word: *por*.

examples.en: Thank you so much for coming.

examples.es:
Gracias por venir.
Con mucho gusto.

rule:
To say what the thanks are for, add *por* and then the thing: *gracias por la ayuda*, *gracias por todo*.

For an action, *por* takes the plain form of the verb, the one ending in *-ar*, *-er* or *-ir*: *gracias por venir*, *gracias por esperar*. English uses the -ing form here (coming, waiting); Spanish never does.

To turn it up, say *muchas gracias por…* or the very Colombian *mil gracias por…* (a thousand thanks). Never *muy gracias*.

The replies you already know still work: *de nada*, *con mucho gusto*, *a la orden*.
smallPrint: Here *por* gives the reason behind the thanks. Teachers call this *por* of cause; *por* has other jobs you'll meet later.

yourTurn.prompt: Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: Gracias ___ la ayuda. (por / para)
Fill the gap and type the whole sentence: Gracias por ___. (venir / vienes) Thanks for coming.
yourTurn.why: After *por* the verb stays in its plain form: *venir*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say: Thank you very much for waiting.
yourTurn.why: *Muchas gracias*, then *por* and the plain verb *esperar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it the Colombian way: Thanks a million for everything.
yourTurn.why: *Mil gracias* is the Colombian way to say thanks a million, and *todo* is everything.
Calling is an action, so it's the plain verb: *llamar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it stronger with *muchas*: Gracias por venir.
yourTurn.why: *Muchas* goes in front of *gracias*; the rest stays the same.

yourTurn.prompt: Thank Don Hernando for the help, with his name at the end.
yourTurn.answer: Gracias por la ayuda, don Hernando.
accept: Muchas gracias por la ayuda, don Hernando.
Mil gracias por la ayuda, don Hernando.
yourTurn.why: The thing you're thankful for comes after *por*: *la ayuda*.

pitfalls.why: Almost. *Gracias* is a noun, so it takes *muchas*, not *muy*.
Close. After *por*, the verb stays in its plain form: *venir*, not *vienes*.
Nearly. English says "for" both ways, but thanks always take *por*.

personal: Think of someone who helped you this week. Write them two thank-you lines with *gracias por*: one for a thing, one for something they did.
